text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Chinese authorities confirm purchase of 30 Airbus and five ATR 72, consider Franco-Chinese co-operation on a 100-seat aircraft.

-- Former European Commission president Jacques Delors calls in an interview for the future European central bank to the balanced by an economic government in which labour ministers would be as powerful as finance ministers.
-- SNCF railway operator and Air France hit by labour conflicts likely to disrupt traffic today and over the weekend.
-- Schneider considers alliances, notably in the U.S.

-- Small and medium-sized firm chiefs support the centre-right coalition in the upcoming parliamentary election, but 46 percent of those polled do not want Alain Juppe to remain Prime Minister, survey shows.
-- Industrialists skeptical about French economic pickup.
-- Paribas seen needing to build strategic alliances to fend off competitors.
-- Supermarkets group Auchan to re-organise Docks de France, merge activities before end 1998.
-- Supermarkets group Leclerc wins court case against competitor Carrefour on brand ownership.
-- Leading French politicians praise American-style capitalism.
-- Detectives raided Paris headquarters of Elf Aquitaine in connection with a fraud enquiry.
